translation.tgt_text: She is the first woman mentioned in the histo­ry of Haiti.

translation.tgt_text: She was the sister of Bohéchio, the Cacique of Xaragwa, kasika located in the south-east of Haiti.

translation.tgt_text: Anacaona married Cacique Caonabo who ruled the Maguana, in the central region of the island.

src_text: "Anakawona se te madanm Kawonabo yon lòt Kasik ki te alatèt Magwana, nan rejyon santral zile a." (Anakawona was the wife of Kawonabo, another chief who led Magwana in the island’s central region.)

translation.src_text: Men sa ki pi enpòtan pou nou konnen sèke Anakawona te renmen anpil anpil lavi atis.
translation.tgt_text: It must be remembered that Anacaona loved the life of an artist very much.

src_text: Men sa ki pi enpòtan pou nou konnen sèke Anakawona te renmen anpil anpil lavi atis. (What’s most important for us to know is that Anakawona deeply loved the life of an artist.)

translation.src_text: Anriyèt Senmak
translation.tgt_text: Henriette Saint-Marc

src_text: Anriyèt Senmak (a Saint-Marc woman)

translation.src_text: Bèl bèl fanm, bèl edikasyon, moun debyen.
translation.tgt_text: A beautiful woman, well-educated, with an impeccable reputation ,

src_text: "Bèl bèl fanm, bèl edikasyon, moun debyen." (Beautiful women, good education, and decent people.)

translation.src_text: Anriyèt deside pase yon kwa sou tout kalite sa yo,
translation.tgt_text: Henriette decided to  set aside these fine qualities.

src_text: "Anriyèt deside pase yon kwa sou tout kalite sa yo," (Anriette decided to put all those things behind her.)

translation.src_text: jete tèt li nan batay pou ride nou kreye yon peyi lib e endepandan.
translation.tgt_text: She threw her body and soul into the struggle for our liberation, to help create a free and independent country.

translation.src_text: Se konsa li te pran desizyon pou l ale vire lòlòj sòlda franse yo pou li vòlè minisyon yo pou pote bay lame endijèn nan.
translation.tgt_text: She took it upon herself to woo the French sol­diers in order to steal ammunition that the native army badly needed.

src_text: "Se konsa li te pran desizyon pou l ale vire lòlòj sòlda franse yo pou li vòlè minisyon yo pou pote bay lame endijèn nan." (So he decided to go distract the French soldiers so he could steal their ammunition and bring it to the indigenous army.)

translation.src_text: Te gen lòt Ayisyèn vanyan ki te konn fè travay sa a tou.
translation.tgt_text: Other courageous Haitians also played this game.

src_text: Te gen lòt Ayisyèn vanyan ki te konn fè travay sa a tou. (There were other brave Haitian women who used to do this work too.)

translation.src_text: Se avèk anpil prekosyon, avèk anpil mètdam pifò nan yo te konn al jwe jwèt difisil sa a pou yo pa kite yo kenbe yo.
translation.tgt_text: However, it was necessa­ry to act with caution, with skill, to avoid being caught.

src_text: "Se avèk anpil prekosyon, avèk anpil mètdam pifò nan yo te konn al jwe jwèt difisil sa a pou yo pa kite yo kenbe yo." (They used to go play this risky game very carefully and with a lot of cunning so they wouldn’t get caught.)

translation.src_text: Malerezman, malgre tout prekosyon li te pran, Anriyèt te fè yo kenbe l.
translation.tgt_text: Unfortunately, despite all the precautions she took, Henriette was discovered.

src_text: "Malerezman, malgre tout prekosyon li te pran, Anriyèt te fè yo kenbe l." (Unfortunately, despite all the precautions he took, Henriette still got him caught.)

translation.src_text: Nan mwa desanm 1802, nan lokalite Depre, David Troy, yon ajan sekrè lame Lafrans, te jwe jwèt tonbe damou pou manmzèl epi mete lapat sou li.
translation.tgt_text: In December 1802, in the district of Depre, Da­vid Troy, a secret agent of the French army, beat Henriette at her own game.  He claimed to be in love with her. In the end, he had her handcuffed.

src_text: "Nan mwa desanm 1802, nan lokalite Depre, David Troy, yon ajan sekrè lame Lafrans, te jwe jwèt tonbe damou pou manmzèl epi mete lapat sou li." (In December 1802, in the area of Depre, David Troy, a secret agent for the French army, played the love game with the young woman and then put the cuffs on her.)

translation.src_text: Li fè minote l, li fè trennen l devan Katedral Pòtoprens pou yo trangle l.
translation.tgt_text: He had her dragged in front of the cathedral of Port-au-Prince to be hanged there.

translation.src_text: Men, anvan Anriyèt mouri li te gentan di kèk bèl pawòl pou mete dife nan kè solda endijèn yo, pou ankouraje yo, mobilize yo.
translation.tgt_text: Nonetheless, before her death, Henriette found the strength to utter courageous words that set fire within the hearts of the native soldiers. With her words, she encouraged them to conti­nue the struggle.

src_text: "Men, anvan Anriyèt mouri li te gentan di kèk bèl pawòl pou mete dife nan kè solda endijèn yo, pou ankouraje yo, mobilize yo." (But before Henriette died, she had already spoken some powerful words to ignite the hearts of the native soldiers, to encourage them and rally them.)

translation.src_text: Dènye rèl Anriyèt la te sèvi kouwè yon kleren majik ki chofe nanm tout esklav revòlte, tout afranchi revolisyonè.
translation.tgt_text: Henriette's last cry was akin to a powerful rhum that would warm the souls of all the rebellious slaves and freedmen that had joi­ned in revolution.

src_text: "Dènye rèl Anriyèt la te sèvi kouwè yon kleren majik ki chofe nanm tout esklav revòlte, tout afranchi revolisyonè." (Henriette’s final cry acted like a magical rum that warmed the souls of all the rebel slaves and revolutionary freed people.)

translation.src_text: Sakrifis Anriyèt la pa t pou granmèsi :
translation.tgt_text: Henriette's sacrifice was not in vain.

src_text: Sakrifis Anriyèt la pa t pou granmèsi : (Anriette’s sacrifice was not for nothing.)

translation.src_text: Yon lane pa t pase lame endijèn te libere Ayiti, kraze lame fransèz, sonnen lanbi pou dezyèm repiblik endepandan nan tout amerik la.
translation.tgt_text: Less than a year la­ter, the native army crushed Napoleon’s army, libe­rating Haiti.

src_text: "Yon lane pa t pase lame endijèn te libere Ayiti, kraze lame fransèz, sonnen lanbi pou dezyèm repiblik endepandan nan tout amerik la." (Within a year, the indigenous army had liberated Haiti, defeated the French army, and sounded the conch shell for the second independent republic in all the Americas.)

translation.tgt_text: She was the penultimate of a family of ten children.

translation.tgt_text: People who knew her said that Ertha was a calm and quiet teenager who liked soli­ tude.

translation.src_text: Se te premye fanm ki te avoka, premye fanm ki te manm bawo Pòtoprens, premye fanm Jij nan peyi Dayiti, premye fanm nan Kou Kasasyon, premye fanm Prezidan peyi nou.
translation.tgt_text: She became the first female lawyer mem­ ber of the Port-au-Prince bar, the first woman judge in Haiti, the first female at the Court of Cas­ sation, the first female president of Haiti.

translation.tgt_text: In 1973, Ertha married Ernst Trouillot, a great lawyer, writer, journalist, and a daughter was born through this union.

src_text: "Nan lane 1973, Ertha te marye avèk Ernst Trouillot yon gran avoka, ekriven, jounalis. Li gen yon pitit fi." (In 1973, Ertha married Ernst Trouillot, a prominent lawyer, writer, and journalist. She has a daughter.)

translation.tgt_text: In 1972, Ertha Pascal Trouillot and her hus­ band published the" Codes de Lois usuelles," an important piece of legal work that most lawyers referred to in our Haitians' court system.

src_text: "Nan lane 1972 Madan Ertha Pascal Trouillot te pibliye avèk mari li yon liv enpòtan « Codes de lois usuelles »." (In 1972, Madam Ertha Pascal Trouillot published an important book with her husband, "Codes de lois usuelles.")

translation.src_text: Nan lane 1990 li soti tòm II «Codes de lois usuelles» Madan Trouillot te ekri lòt liv ankò, pou pi piti 4 liv.  Ertha Pascal Trouillot te prezidan nou 13 mas 1990.

translation.tgt_text: It was not easy, but Ertha succee­ded in having honest elections, democratic, cre­ dible values that Haiti did not have long ago.

translation.tgt_text: Former President Ertha Pascal now lives at her residential home, writing books, presenting lec­ tures, and advising her sisters and brothers to live their faith.

translation.tgt_text: We want to close with this judicious advice offered to us by President Ertha Pascale Trouillot.

src_text: "Se konsa n ap fini avèk bèl konsèy sa a, Prezidan Ertha te sere pou nou:" (So this is how we’ll wrap up with this beautiful advice President Ertha had in store for us:)

src_text: Se konsa li rantre nan televizyon « Radyo-Kanada » (That’s how he ended up on Radio-Canada TV).

translation.src_text: Li patisipe nan plizyè emisyon pou okipe yon plas nan kè tout Kanadyen.
translation.tgt_text: She appeared on several shows and won a spe­ cial place in the hearts of all Canadians.

src_text: Li patisipe nan plizyè emisyon pou okipe yon plas nan kè tout Kanadyen. (He took part in several shows to win a place in the hearts of all Canadians.)

translation.src_text: Li patisipe nan plizyè film nan kolaborasyon avèk mari li Daniel Lafond.
translation.tgt_text: She has participated in the making of several films in col­ laboration with her husband, Daniel Lafond.

src_text: Li patisipe nan plizyè film nan kolaborasyon avèk mari li Daniel Lafond. (She took part in several films in collaboration with her husband, Daniel Lafond.)

translation.tgt_text: She has also participated in several programs in Haiti.

src_text: Li patisipe nan plizyè emisyon sou Ayiti : (He took part in several programs about Haiti.)

translation.src_text: Nan repòtaj eleksyon 1987 li manke pèdi lavi l anba bal atoufè nan Pòtoprens.
translation.tgt_text: On the occasion of the report on the elections of 1987, she almost lost her life under the bandits' bullets in Port-au-Prince.

src_text: "Nan repòtaj eleksyon 1987 li manke pèdi lavi l anba bal atoufè nan Pòtoprens." (During the 1987 election coverage, he nearly lost his life to a stray bullet in Port-au-Prince.)

translation.src_text: Paske li pa te kapab fè pitit, li te vini Ayiti pou adopte yon ti fi :
translation.tgt_text: Because she could not have children, she came to Haiti to adopt a daughter:

src_text: Paske li pa te kapab fè pitit, li te vini Ayiti pou adopte yon ti fi : (Because she couldn’t have children, she came to Haiti to adopt a little girl.)

translation.tgt_text: She understands Portuguese.

src_text: "Kòm benevòl li te renmen bay tan li pou ede fanm ki nan pwoblèm, timoun ki nan mizè." (As a volunteer, he loved giving his time to help women in trouble and children in hardship.)

translation.tgt_text: She has received more than 10 decorations and honors.

src_text: Li resevwa pase 10 dekorasyon ak distenksyon onorifik. (He received more than 10 decorations and honorary distinctions.)

translation.src_text: Jedi 4 out 2005, lakataw fè taw nan tout Kanada.
translation.tgt_text: On Thursday, August 4, 2005, it was a thun­ derclap in Canada.

src_text: "Jedi 4 out 2005, lakataw fè taw nan tout Kanada." (On Thursday, August 4, 2005, the whole of Canada was buzzing with excitement.)

translation.src_text: Premye Minis Kanadyen an Paul Martin anonse nominasyon Michaëlle Jean kòm Gouvènè Jeneral peyi Kanada.
translation.tgt_text: Canadian Prime Minister Paul Martin announces the appointment of Michaëlle Jean as Governor-General of Canada.

src_text: "Premye Minis Kanadyen an Paul Martin anonse nominasyon Michaëlle Jean kòm Gouvènè Jeneral peyi Kanada." (Canadian Prime Minister Paul Martin announced Michaëlle Jean’s appointment as Governor General of Canada.)

translation.src_text: Se yon gwo reskonsabilite ak yon gran lonè pou Michaëlle.
translation.tgt_text: It is a great responsibility and a great honor for Michaëlle.

src_text: Se yon gwo reskonsabilite ak yon gran lonè pou Michaëlle. (It’s a great responsibility and a great honor for Michaëlle.)

translation.src_text: Men tou se fyète ak lonè pou Ayiti ki gen yon pitit li ki pral okipe plas onorifik ki pi enpòtan nan Kanada.
translation.tgt_text: It was also pride and honor for Haiti to have one of her children occupy this prestigious position, the most important in Canada.

src_text: "Men tou se fyète ak lonè pou Ayiti ki gen yon pitit li ki pral okipe plas onorifik ki pi enpòtan nan Kanada." (It is also a source of pride and honor for Haiti to have one of its children take on one of the most important honorary positions in Canada.)

translation.src_text: Paske pòs Gouvènè Jeneral la se :
translation.tgt_text: Because the position of Governor-General consists of:

src_text: Paske pòs Gouvènè Jeneral la se : (Because the office of Governor-General is:)

translation.src_text: - reprezante Rèn Angletè a nan Kanada avèk tit kòmandan-chèf lame Kanada a;
translation.tgt_text: - represent the Queen of England in Canada, with the title of Commander-in-Chief of the Cana­ dian Army;

src_text: - reprezante Rèn Angletè a nan Kanada avèk tit kòmandan-chèf lame Kanada a; (represents the Queen of England in Canada with the title of Commander-in-Chief of the Canadian Armed Forces)

translation.src_text: - vizite militè kanadyen yo ki nan peyi etranje epi remèt yo dekorasyon;
translation.tgt_text: - visit and present decorations to Canadian mi­ litary personnel abroad;

src_text: - vizite militè kanadyen yo ki nan peyi etranje epi remèt yo dekorasyon; (visit the Canadian troops stationed abroad and present them with their decorations)

translation.src_text: - fè pwomosyon inite nan Kanada ki gen 10 pwovens plis twa teritwa;
translation.tgt_text: - promote unity in Canada, which has 10 pro­ vinces and three territories;

src_text: - fè pwomosyon inite nan Kanada ki gen 10 pwovens plis twa teritwa; (promote unity in Canada, which has 10 provinces and 3 territories)

translation.src_text: - aprann Kanadyen yo pou yo fyè peyi yo Kanada epi pou yo travay mete kanpe kominote djanm ki gen kè nan men;
translation.tgt_text: - teach Canadians to be proud of their country, Canada;

src_text: - aprann Kanadyen yo pou yo fyè peyi yo Kanada epi pou yo travay mete kanpe kominote djanm ki gen kè nan men; (teach Canadians to be proud of their country, Canada, and to work together to build strong communities with heart)

translation.src_text: - disoud palman an ouben mande chèf opozisyon an pou fòme yon nouvo gouvènman lè sa nesesè;
translation.tgt_text: teach them how to work to build a strong and generous community;

src_text: - disoud palman an ouben mande chèf opozisyon an pou fòme yon nouvo gouvènman lè sa nesesè; (dissolve parliament or ask the opposition leader to form a new government when necessary)

translation.src_text: - prezide seremoni asèmantasyon Premye Minis, Jij chèf kousiprèm, konsèy minis yo;
translation.tgt_text: - dissolve parliament or ask the opposition lea­ der to form a new government if necessary;

src_text: - prezide seremoni asèmantasyon Premye Minis, Jij chèf kousiprèm, konsèy minis yo; (preside over the swearing-in ceremony of the Prime Minister, the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, and the Council of Ministers)

translation.src_text: - resevwa lèt kreyans anbasadè ki vin reprezante peyi yo nan Kanada;
translation.tgt_text: - preside over the swearing-in ceremony of the Prime Minister, the President of the Supreme Court, the Council of Ministers;

src_text: - resevwa lèt kreyans anbasadè ki vin reprezante peyi yo nan Kanada; (receive the letters of credence from ambassadors who have come to represent their countries in Canada)

translation.src_text: Gouvènè Michaëlle ap gen 2 rezidans ofisyèl :
translation.tgt_text: - receive credentials from ambassadors repre­ senting their country in Canada;

src_text: "Gouvènè Michaëlle ap gen 2 rezidans ofisyèl :" (Governor Michaëlle will have two official residences:)

translation.src_text: yon palè nan mitan yon pak 32 ekta bwaze ak 10 000 pyebwa nan Otawa kapital federal la, nan pwovens Ontaryo;
translation.tgt_text: Governor Michaëlle will have 2 official resi­ dences:

src_text: "yon palè nan mitan yon pak 32 ekta bwaze ak 10 000 pyebwa nan Otawa kapital federal la, nan pwovens Ontaryo;" (a palace in the middle of a 32-hectare wooded park with 10,000 trees in Ottawa, the federal capital, in Ontario;)

translation.src_text: ak yon lòt palè nan vil Kebèk ki se kapital Pwovens Kebèk la tou:
translation.tgt_text: a palace in the middle of a 32-acre park with 10,000 trees in the federal capital Ottawa, in the province of Ontario,

src_text: ak yon lòt palè nan vil Kebèk ki se kapital Pwovens Kebèk la tou: (and another palace in Quebec City, which is also the capital of Quebec Province:)

translation.src_text: chato Lasitadèl nan plèn Abraham.
translation.tgt_text: and another palace in Quebec, capital of the province of Quebec:

src_text: "chato Lasitadèl nan plèn Abraham." (the Citadelle castle on the Plain of Abraham)

translation.src_text: Michaëlle Jean Gouvènè Jeneral gen yon drapo ki gen premye plas, devan drapo kanadyen.
translation.tgt_text: the Château La Citadelle on the Plains of Abraham.

src_text: "Michaëlle Jean Gouvènè Jeneral gen yon drapo ki gen premye plas, devan drapo kanadyen." (Michaëlle Jean, as Governor General, has a flag that takes the place of honor ahead of the Canadian flag.)

translation.src_text: L ap gen 170 moun sou zòd li pou ba li tout sèvis li bezwen nan travay Gouvènè li.
translation.tgt_text: The flag of the Governor-General, in this case, Michaëlle Jean, occupies the first place in front of the Canadian flag.

src_text: L ap gen 170 moun sou zòd li pou ba li tout sèvis li bezwen nan travay Gouvènè li. (He will have 170 people under his command to provide all the support he needs in his role as Governor.)

translation.src_text: Anplis salè pèsonèl li, li kapab itilize yon bidjè 19 milyon dola kanadyen, toujou pou bezwen travay Gouvènè li.
translation.tgt_text: The Governor will have 170 people under him to provide him with all the ser­ vices he needs for his work.

src_text: "Anplis salè pèsonèl li, li kapab itilize yon bidjè 19 milyon dola kanadyen, toujou pou bezwen travay Gouvènè li." (In addition to his personal salary, he can also use a 19 million Canadian dollar budget, still for the needs of his Governor’s work.)

translation.src_text: Apre tan Michaelle Jean pase nan travay gouvènè jeneral nan peyi Kanada, li te okipe pòs sila yo :
translation.tgt_text: In addition to her per­ sonal salary, she has a $ 19 million budget for her governor.

src_text: Apre tan Michaelle Jean pase nan travay gouvènè jeneral nan peyi Kanada, li te okipe pòs sila yo : (After Michaëlle Jean served as Governor General of Canada, she held these positions:)

translation.src_text: • Anvwaye espesyal pou INESKO nan peyi AYITI (1e Oktòb 2010).
translation.tgt_text: After his tenure as Governor-General of Cana­ da, Michael Jean held the following positions:

translation.tgt_text: • Special Envoy for UNESCO in HAITI (October 1, 2010);

src_text: • Prezidan Konsèy Administrasyon Enstiti Wotzetid Kebèk nan Inivèsite Laval (October 2010).

src_text: • Chanselye Inivèsite OTAWA (Chancellor of the University of Ottawa, November 7, 2011).

translation.src_text: • Temwen Òganizasyon Entènasyonal Frankofoni nan Je Olenpik nan kapital peyi Angletè, Lond (Avril 2011).
translation.tgt_text: • Chancellor of the University of OTTAWA (No­ vember 7, 2011);

src_text: • Temwen Òganizasyon Entènasyonal Frankofoni nan Je Olenpik nan kapital peyi Angletè, Lond (April 2011).

src_text: • Sekretè Jeneral OIF (Òganizasyon Entènasyonal Frankofoni) (20 Novanm 2014). (Secretary General of the OIF, the International Organization of La Francophonie, November 20, 2014.)

translation.src_text: Mari Michèl ap di nou kouman li rive pèdi janm li:
translation.tgt_text: Marie Michelle tells us how she lost her legs:

src_text: "Mari Michèl ap di nou kouman li rive pèdi janm li:" (Mary Michel is telling us how he ended up losing his leg:)

translation.src_text: “M te lakay avèk Leyanda, ti nyès mwen ki gen twazan.
translation.tgt_text: "I was at the house with Leyanda, my three year old niece.

src_text: “M te lakay avèk Leyanda, ti nyès mwen ki gen twazan.” (I was at home with Leyanda, my little niece who is three years old.)

translation.src_text: Lè kay la tranble a, tout mi yo tonbe.
translation.tgt_text: When the house shook, during the earth­ quake, all the walls collapsed.

src_text: "Lè kay la tranble a, tout mi yo tonbe." (When the house shakes, all the walls fall down.)

translation.src_text: Mwen kouri jwenn Leyanda
translation.tgt_text: I ran towards Leyan­ da.

src_text: Mwen kouri jwenn Leyanda (I rushed to go see Leyanda)

translation.src_text: epi mwen pwoteje li avèk kò mwen.
translation.tgt_text: I was protecting her with my body.

src_text: "epi mwen pwoteje li avèk kò mwen." (and I protect it with my own body.)

translation.src_text: Anpil gravwa te kouvri mwen.
translation.tgt_text: The rubble had almost buried me.

src_text: Anpil gravwa te kouvri mwen. (I was weighed down by many burdens.)

translation.src_text: M pa te ka bouje.
translation.tgt_text: I couldn't move.

src_text: M pa te ka bouje. (I couldn’t move.)

translation.src_text: M te santi anpil doulè.
translation.tgt_text: I felt a lot of pain.

src_text: M te santi anpil doulè. (I felt a lot of pain.)

translation.src_text: Epi Leyanda te gen anpil perèz.
translation.tgt_text: And Leyanda was very afraid.

src_text: Epi Leyanda te gen anpil perèz. (And Leyanda was very scared.)

translation.src_text: Mwen sere li pi fò epi mwen pa sispann pale avèk li, yon jan pou mwen ba li konfyans.
translation.tgt_text: I hugged her very tightly and kept talking to her, to give her confidence.

src_text: Mwen sere li pi fò epi mwen pa sispann pale avèk li, yon jan pou mwen ba li konfyans. (I kept it to myself even more and kept talking to him, so I could build trust.)

translation.src_text: Nou rete konsa tout nwit la”.
translation.tgt_text: We stayed like that all night.

src_text: "Nou rete konsa tout nwit la” (We stayed up like that all night).

translation.src_text: Leyanda sòti anba dekonm yo san yon ti blese.
translation.tgt_text: Leyanda emerged from the rubble unharmed.

src_text: "Leyanda sòti anba dekonm yo san yon ti blese." (Leyanda came out from under the rubble without even a scratch.)

translation.src_text: Men Mari Michèl te gen janm dwat li krabouye.
translation.tgt_text: But Marie Michelle’s right leg was in bad shape.

src_text: Men Mari Michèl te gen janm dwat li krabouye. (But Mary Michel had her right leg crushed.)

translation.src_text: Lè nou te rankontre li, li t ap soufri ak doulè.
translation.tgt_text: When we met her, she was in great pain.

src_text: Lè nou te rankontre li, li t ap soufri ak doulè. (When we met him, he was suffering from pain.)

translation.src_text: Men li te tenn fas ap pote rekonfò bay lòt blese ak fanmi yo.
translation.tgt_text: But, she had stood up to comfort other wounded and their families.

src_text: Men li te tenn fas ap pote rekonfò bay lòt blese ak fanmi yo. (But there he was, stoic and composed, offering comfort to the injured and their families.)

translation.src_text: “Wi, mwen tris, men mwen jwenn tout fanmi mwen.
translation.tgt_text: “Yes, I'm sad, but I found all my fa­ mily.

src_text: Wi, mwen tris, men mwen jwenn tout fanmi mwen. (Yes, I’m sad, but I found all my family.)

translation.src_text: Mwen sove ti nyès mwen an.
translation.tgt_text: I saved my little niece.

src_text: Mwen sove ti nyès mwen an. (I saved my little niece.)

translation.src_text: Epi mwen gen lavi devan mwen.
translation.tgt_text: And I have life in front of me.

src_text: Epi mwen gen lavi devan mwen. (And I still have my whole life ahead of me.)

translation.src_text: Sa mwen swete se yon pwotèz pou mwen retounen lekòl epi yon jou vini otèsdelè”.
translation.tgt_text: I want to have a prosthetic leg to go back to school and one day become a flight attendant ”.

src_text: "Sa mwen swete se yon pwotèz pou mwen retounen lekòl epi yon jou vini otèsdelè” (What I hope for is to get a prosthesis so I can go back to school and one day become an air hostess)."

translation.src_text: Èmit se yon ti restavèk.
translation.tgt_text: Hermit is a small "restavèk".

src_text: Èmit se yon ti restavèk. (Émit is like a little servant child.)

translation.src_text: Gen katran depi manman li te bay li pou li te kapab gen yon lavi miyò.
translation.tgt_text: It has been four years since her mother placed her in domestic ser­ vice so that she could have a better life.

src_text: "Gen katran depi manman li te bay li pou li te kapab gen yon lavi miyò." (It’s been four years since his mother gave him up so he could have a better life.)

translation.src_text: Men ki lavi miyò?
translation.tgt_text: But, what better life?

src_text: "Men ki lavi miyò?" (But what better life is there?)

translation.src_text: Chak jou se baton, travay san pran souf ak grangou.
translation.tgt_text: Everyday she collects beatings, does many chores, and is pained by hunger.

src_text: "Chak jou se baton, travay san pran souf ak grangou." (Every day is a struggle, working nonstop while hungry.)

translation.src_text: Depi latè a tranble, bagay yo vin pi di pou li.
translation.tgt_text: Since the earthquake, life has become even more difficult for her.

src_text: "Depi latè a tranble, bagay yo vin pi di pou li." (Once the ground starts shaking, things get harder for him.)

translation.src_text: Si li dòmi deyò, si lamanjay vin pi ra se li yo voye fouye anba dekonm.
translation.tgt_text: If she sleeps outside, if food is scarce, she still has to go digging under the rubble.

src_text: "Si li dòmi deyò, si lamanjay vin pi ra se li yo voye fouye anba dekonm." (If he sleeps outside, and food becomes scarce, he’s the one they send to dig through the rubble.)

translation.src_text: “Se mwen yo voye chak jou andedan kay kraze a al chache kèk bagay.
translation.tgt_text: "Every day I have to go to the ruined house to collect whatever I can find.

src_text: “Se mwen yo voye chak jou andedan kay kraze a al chache kèk bagay.” (It’s me they send every day into the ruined house to go look for a few things.)

translation.src_text: Se gwo danje.
translation.tgt_text: It's very dangerous.

src_text: Se gwo danje. (It’s a serious danger.)

translation.src_text: Mwen pè.
translation.tgt_text: I'm afraid.

src_text: Mwen pè. (I’m scared.)

translation.src_text: Men mwen oblije ale.
translation.tgt_text: But I have to go.

src_text: Men mwen oblije ale. (But I have to go.)

translation.src_text: ” * * * Starling gen 8 lane.
translation.tgt_text: " * * * Starling is 8 years old.

src_text: Starling gen 8 lane. (Starling is 8 years old.)

translation.src_text: Avèk paran li, li jwenn refij nan lakou Primati a.
translation.tgt_text: With her parents, she found refuge in the courtyard of the Prime Minis­ ter.

src_text: "Avèk paran li, li jwenn refij nan lakou Primati a." (With his parents, he finds refuge in the Prime Minister’s compound.)

translation.src_text: Se la l ap jwe avèk nouvo zanmi li fèk fè yo.
translation.tgt_text: There she plays with her new friends.

src_text: "Se la l ap jwe avèk nouvo zanmi li fèk fè yo." (That’s where he’s hanging out with the new friends he just made.)

translation.src_text: L ap jwe, konsa li ka rive bliye pou yon ti moman lavi di ki genyen depi latè tranble a.
translation.tgt_text: She plays, so she can forget for a moment the hard life she has led since the earthquake.

src_text: "L ap jwe, konsa li ka rive bliye pou yon ti moman lavi di ki genyen depi latè tranble a." (He’s playing, so he can forget for a moment the hard life that’s been there since the earthquake.)

translation.src_text: “Jou sa a m t ap fè devwa mwen sou balkon lakay.
translation.tgt_text: “That day I was doing my homework on the balcony at home.

src_text: “Jou sa a m t ap fè devwa mwen sou balkon lakay.” (That day, I was doing my homework on the balcony at home.)

translation.src_text: Papa m te nan travay.
translation.tgt_text: My father was at work.

src_text: Papa m te nan travay. (My dad was at work.)

translation.src_text: Manman m te ale nan makèt.
translation.tgt_text: My mother had gone shop­ ping ...

src_text: Manman m te ale nan makèt. (My mom went to the market.)

translation.src_text: Wòch, grava tonbe sou kaye mwen, sou liv mwen.
translation.tgt_text: Rocks and rubble reopened my notebook and my book.

src_text: "Wòch, grava tonbe sou kaye mwen, sou liv mwen." (Rocks and gravel fell on my notebook, on my book.)

translation.src_text: M te kon yon egare.
translation.tgt_text: I was there, dazed ...

src_text: M te kon yon egare. (I used to be such a fool.)

translation.src_text: Lè m gade,
translation.tgt_text: Finally, I un­ derstood ...

src_text: Lè m gade, (when I look around,)

translation.src_text: kay la te kraze epi m te nan mitan dekonm”.
translation.tgt_text: the house had collapsed and I found myself in the middle of the rubble.

src_text: "kay la te kraze epi m te nan mitan dekonm" (the house had collapsed, and I was left in the middle of the rubble).

translation.src_text: Nan jaden Primati a, gen yon gwo kan refijye.
translation.tgt_text: In the garden of the Prime Minister, there is a large refugee camp.

src_text: "Nan jaden Primati a, gen yon gwo kan refijye." (In Primati’s yard, there’s a huge refugee camp.)

translation.src_text: Yon kan ki la pou dire epi ki kapab fè kèk jou anvan refijye yo deplase.
translation.tgt_text: A camp which will probably stand for some time, until the refugees are able to leave.

src_text: "Yon kan ki la pou dire epi ki kapab fè kèk jou anvan refijye yo deplase." (A camp meant to last and able to hold for a few days before the refugees move on.)

translation.src_text: Akote bougenvilye yo, anba flanbwayan yo ou jwenn tant yo, tonèl yo, ak pwela yo ki aliyen kòrekteman.

translation.tgt_text: They find themselves in a united family, a good example to follow.

translation.src_text: Nan tout istwa foutbòl fanm, se premye fwa yon ekip fanm nan Karayib la, Ayiti, te kalifye pou FIFA nan kategori mwens pase 20 lane.
translation.tgt_text: U-20 Historically, too, this is the first time that a Ca­ ribbean women's team, in this case Haiti, has qua­ lified for the Fifa World Cup in the under-20 cate­ gory.

src_text: "Nan tout istwa foutbòl fanm, se premye fwa yon ekip fanm nan Karayib la, Ayiti, te kalifye pou FIFA nan kategori mwens pase 20 lane." (In the whole history of women’s soccer, this is the first time a women’s team from the Caribbean—Haiti—has qualified for FIFA in the under-20 category.)

translation.src_text: Nan zòn CONCACAF la se toujou ekip fanm ki sòti nan Amerik di Nò, ki ap domine sitou ekip Etazini an, li pa janm fè yon match nul, ni pèdi yon match.
translation.tgt_text: The Concacaf zone is still dominated by the women's teams from North America, mainly that of the United States of America, which had never drawn or lost a match (in several confrontations) in the regional semi-final, qualifying for the world cup.

src_text: "Nan zòn CONCACAF la se toujou ekip fanm ki sòti nan Amerik di Nò, ki ap domine sitou ekip Etazini an, li pa janm fè yon match nul, ni pèdi yon match." (In the CONCACAF region, it’s always the women’s teams from North America that dominate, especially the U.S. team; they never draw or lose a match.)

(Often, when two people live in the same house for a long time, they eventually reach a point where the old feelings fade and habit takes over.)

translation.src_text: Men si pou santiman yo retounen monte teren an nèf kou nèf pwen, fòk tou de (2) mounn yo rebati frechè jenès yo nan lavi lanmou yo.
translation.tgt_text: But for the feeling to come back and prepare the soil to make things bright and new, the two (2) people must rebuild the freshness of their youth in their days of love.

src_text: "Men si pou santiman yo retounen monte teren an nèf kou nèf pwen, fòk tou de (2) mounn yo rebati frechè jenès yo nan lavi lanmou yo." (But if those feelings are going to come back strong and start fresh again, both people have to rebuild the spark of their youth in their love life.)

translation.src_text: Se poutèt sa, jodi a mwen vle di ou mwen toujou renmen ou, ep1 mwen vle fè ou santi tout chalè lanmou k'ap debobinen nan kè m' pou ou.
translation.tgt_text: This is why today I want to tell you I love you still andiwant to make you feel the radiance of all the love unwinding from my heart for you.

src_text: Se poutèt sa, jodi a mwen vle di ou mwen toujou renmen ou, ep1 mwen vle fè ou santi tout chalè lanmou k'ap debobinen nan kè m' pou ou. (That’s why, today I want to tell you that I still love you, and I want you to feel all the warmth of the love that keeps flowing from my heart for you.)

translation.src_text: Jodi a lespri ou sele-m pandan tout lajounen an, li pa bay bonnanj mwen souf pou li pran youn kanpo. Lòloj mwen tèlman ap bay sakad pou ou, se kòm si nou te chita kotakòt, kou kòkòt ak figaro, nan pye mòn lopital, kote lanmou younn te tanmen tire tèt pou lòt.
translation.tgt_text: Today your spirit rode me all day long, it didn't give my soul breath to take a rest. My clock is so rocked by you it's as if we were still sitting side by side at the foot of Mont Hópital, where love for one reared its head in the other.

src_text: "Jodi a lespri ou sele-m pandan tout lajounen an, li pa bay bonnanj mwen souf pou li pran youn kanpo. Lòloj mwen tèlman ap bay sakad pou ou, se kòm si nou te chita kotakòt, kou kòkòt ak figaro, nan pye mòn lopital, kote lanmou younn te tanmen tire tèt pou lòt." (Today your spirit has been on my mind all day long, not giving my soul a moment’s rest. My heart keeps jolting for you, as if we were sitting side by side, close as can be, at the foot of the hospital hill, where our love had already started leaning toward each other.)

translation.src_text: An nou kite lanmou nou tire tèt toujou, paske se nan tire tèt li pral jwenn van pou li remonte nan lespas larnmou dyougans nou youn lanmou laj pa dwe tenyen.
translation.tgt_text: May our love keep rearing up, because rearing up so, it will find the wind that will carry it up to the space of our youthlul love, which age cannot exinguish.

src_text: "An nou kite lanmou nou tire tèt toujou, paske se nan tire tèt li pral jwenn van pou li remonte nan lespas larnmou dyougans nou youn lanmou laj pa dwe tenyen." (Let our love keep rising above, because it is through that struggle that it will find the wind to lift itself back into the vastness of our love; no matter how old our love grows, it should never be extinguished.)

translation.src_text: Laj ap antre sou nou, se vre, men kap lanmou nou dwe kontinye monte apik nan syèl eksperyans nou kote bwamitan pasyans nou pral fè li gwonde nan youn espas nou va rive kreye pou nou de nan zile jaden kò fanm ou
translation.tgt_text: Age stalks us, its true, but our kite should continue rising straight up in the sky of our experience where the pillar of our patience will make it roar in a space we've Created for us both, in the island garden of your womanly body.

src_text: "Laj ap antre sou nou, se vre, men kap lanmou nou dwe kontinye monte apik nan syèl eksperyans nou kote bwamitan pasyans nou pral fè li gwonde nan youn espas nou va rive kreye pou nou de nan zile jaden kò fanm ou" (Yes, age is catching up with us, but our love must keep climbing steeply through the sky of our shared experiences, where the patience we’ve built will make it roar in the space we create for the two of us in the island-garden of your womanly body)

translation.src_text: Li Pa gen nen nan figi li
translation.tgt_text: An naive person

src_text: Li Pa gen nen nan figi li (He has no shame at all)

translation.src_text: W ap voye flè
translation.tgt_text: You say silly things, you’re not serious about what you’re saying.

src_text: W ap voye flè (you’re throwing flowers around)

translation.src_text: Ti Mari p ap monte, Ti Mari p ap desann
translation.tgt_text: Things will stay the same.

src_text: "Ti Mari p ap monte, Ti Mari p ap desann" (Little Mary isn’t going up, and Little Mary isn’t coming down)

translation.src_text: Yon vyewo li ye wi
translation.tgt_text: he’s a person with experience.

src_text: Yon vyewo li ye wi (He’s an old-timer, you know)

translation.src_text: Abraham di sètase
translation.tgt_text: Enough is enough, I have enough

src_text: "Abraham di sètase" (Abraham said enough is enough)

translation.src_text: Pwoblèm p ap fini
translation.tgt_text: To say when problems seem to accumulate.

src_text: Pwoblèm p ap fini (Problems never end)

translation.src_text: Ban m zorey mwen
translation.tgt_text: Be quiet! Shut up!

src_text: "Ban m zorey mwen" (Let me hear what I need to hear)

translation.src_text: Tann jis nou tounen pwa tann
translation.tgt_text: Wait a long time.

src_text: Tann jis nou tounen pwa tann (Wait until we turn into dried peas)

translation.src_text: Ou ap voye flè
translation.tgt_text: youu are acting up

src_text: Ou ap voye flè (you’re flirting)

translation.src_text: Yon vyewo li ye wi
translation.tgt_text: He’s a “know-it-all”,

src_text: Yon vyewo li ye wi (He’s an old-timer, you know)

translation.src_text: Mande mwen yon ti kou ankò ma di ou
translation.tgt_text: I don’t know,

src_text: "Mande mwen yon ti kou ankò ma di ou" (Ask me again in a little while, and I’ll tell you.)

translation.src_text: Mande mwen yon ti kou ankò ma di ou
translation.tgt_text: Not right now, and honestly, I don’t have an answer for you.

src_text: Mande mwen yon ti kou ankò ma di ou (Ask me again in a little while, and I’ll tell you.)

translation.src_text: M ap degaje mwen kom Mèt Jean-Jacques
translation.tgt_text: I will do my best to get out of it.

src_text: M ap degaje mwen kom Mèt Jean-Jacques (I’m making do on my own, like Master Jean-Jacques)

translation.src_text: Pwoblèm p ap fini
translation.tgt_text: One hardship follows another

src_text: Pwoblèm p ap fini (Problems never end)

translation.src_text: Mazora
translation.tgt_text: Gap-toothed

src_text: Mazora (a person who is always meddling or stirring up trouble)

translation.src_text: Sife
translation.tgt_text: therefore

src_text: Sife (to be patient and endure)

translation.src_text: Sa blan di la?
translation.tgt_text: What are you talking about?

src_text: Sa blan di la? (What did the white person say there?)

translation.src_text: Pito nou lèd nou la
translation.tgt_text: glad to be alive

src_text: "Pito nou lèd nou la" (Better to be ugly but present than to be absent)

translation.src_text: Ban m zòrèy mwen
translation.tgt_text: stop talking

src_text: "Ban m zòrèy mwen" (Give me my ears back)

translation.src_text: Fòk ou konn la pou ou la
translation.tgt_text: to have experience on the matter, to have knowledge

src_text: "Fòk ou konn la pou ou la" (You have to know the place to really belong there)

translation.src_text: Achte figi
translation.tgt_text: kissing butts

src_text: Achte figi (to save face)

translation.src_text: Pran fil
translation.tgt_text: moving forward in life, to become better

src_text: Pran fil (take the lead)

translation.src_text: Bat lestomak ou twa fwa
translation.tgt_text: don’t go there

src_text: Bat lestomak ou twa fwa (pat your stomach three times)

translation.src_text: Ret nan wòl ou
translation.tgt_text: leave me alone

src_text: Ret nan wòl ou (stay in your lane)

translation.src_text: Ou ap voye flè
translation.tgt_text: you’re messing around

src_text: Ou ap voye flè (you’re flirting)

translation.src_text: M ap ba ou sa sou de chèz
translation.tgt_text: I will give you all the details

src_text: M ap ba ou sa sou de chèz (I’m going to give you that straight, no beating around the bush)

translation.src_text: Pa fè bouch mwen long
translation.tgt_text: don’t make me talk too much

src_text: Pa fè bouch mwen long (Don’t make me look bad)

translation.src_text: Veye zo ou
translation.tgt_text: be careful or watch your back

src_text: Veye zo ou (watch your back)

translation.src_text: Ou ap kouri pou lapli, ou al tonbe nan gran rivyè
translation.tgt_text: you are running from something bad that’s small and then get into something much bigger or dangerous

src_text: Ou ap kouri pou lapli, ou al tonbe nan gran rivyè (You run from the rain only to fall into the big river).

translation.src_text: Mete dlo nan diven ou
translation.tgt_text: calm down

src_text: Mete dlo nan diven ou (dilute your wine)

translation.src_text: Chak jou pa dimanch
translation.tgt_text: you may not get the same results all the time

src_text: Chak jou pa dimanch (Every day isn’t Sunday)

translation.src_text: Se rat kay, k ap manje pay kay
translation.tgt_text: whatever is going wrong is usually being done by someone on the inside

src_text: Se rat kay, k ap manje pay kay (It’s the house rat that eats the house’s straw.)

translation.src_text: Tout lapriyè gen amen
translation.tgt_text: all beginnings have an end

src_text: "Tout lapriyè gen amen" (Every prayer has its amen.)

translation.src_text: Pa jete chodyè ize pou chodyè nèf
translation.tgt_text: don’t get rid of old friends for new ones

src_text: Pa jete chodyè ize pou chodyè nèf (don’t throw away an old pot for a new one)

translation.src_text: Ban m zòrèy mwen
translation.tgt_text: stop making noise

src_text: Ban m zòrèy mwen (Let me hear what you have to say)

translation.src_text: Chak jou pa dimanch
translation.tgt_text: Don’t keep breaking the rules and expect no consequences

src_text: Chak jou pa dimanch (Every day isn’t Sunday)

translation.src_text: Gate san
translation.tgt_text: to be angry

src_text: "Gate san" (to be hot-tempered; to have a bad temper)

translation.src_text: Sak vid pa kanpe
translation.tgt_text: hungry people can’t do much

src_text: Sak vid pa kanpe (An empty sack can’t stand up)

translation.src_text: Santi bon koute chè
translation.tgt_text: work hard for what you want because good things cost a lot of money

src_text: Santi bon koute chè (Looking good costs money)

translation.src_text: Se lave men siye atè
translation.tgt_text: it’s a waste of time

src_text: "Se lave men siye atè" (It’s like washing your hands and then wiping them on the ground)

translation.src_text: Ou konn kouri ou pa konn kache
translation.tgt_text: A guilty person will be caught sooner or later

src_text: Ou konn kouri ou pa konn kache (You know how to run, but you don’t know how to hide)

translation.src_text: Men anpil, chay pa lou.
translation.tgt_text: Many hands [make] the load lighter.

src_text: Men anpil, chay pa lou. (Many hands make light work.)

translation.src_text: Anpil ti patat fè chay.
translation.tgt_text: A lot of small potatoes make a load.

src_text: "Anpil ti patat fè chay." (Many small sweet potatoes can make a load.)

translation.src_text: Aprè dans, tanbou toujou lou.
translation.tgt_text: After the dance, the drums are always heavy.

src_text: Aprè dans, tanbou toujou lou. (After the dance, the drum is always heavy.)

translation.src_text: Avan ou ri moun bwete, gade jan ou mache.
translation.tgt_text: Before you laugh at those who limp, check the way you walk.

src_text: "Avan ou ri moun bwete, gade jan ou mache." (Before you laugh at someone who limps, look at how you walk.)

translation.src_text: Avek pasyans, w’ap wè tete foumi.
translation.tgt_text: With patience, you will see an ant’s breast.

src_text: Avek pasyans, w’ap wè tete foumi. (With patience, you’ll see even the tiniest details.)

translation.src_text: Ayisyen swiv kouran.
translation.tgt_text: Haitians follow the flow.

src_text: Ayisyen swiv kouran. (Haitians go with the flow.)

translation.src_text: Ayiti se tè glise.
translation.tgt_text: Haiti is a sliding land (quicksand).

src_text: Ayiti se tè glise. (Haiti is slippery ground.)

translation.src_text: Bab pi long, men sousi pi vye.
translation.tgt_text: The beard is longer, but the Eyebrows are older.

src_text: "Bab pi long, men sousi pi vye." (A beard may be longer, but a worry is older.)

translation.src_text: Baton ede pye.
translation.tgt_text: The stick helps the foot.

src_text: "Baton ede pye." (A walking stick helps the feet.)

translation.src_text: Bay kou, bliye; pote mak, sonje.
translation.tgt_text: [You] give a blow, [you] forget; [when you] leave marks, [they] remember.

src_text: "Bay kou, bliye; pote mak, sonje." (The one who deals the blow forgets, but the one who bears the scar remembers.)

translation.src_text: Bay piti pa chich.
translation.tgt_text: Giving a little is not stingy.

src_text: Bay piti pa chich. (Even a little gift shouldn’t be stingy.)

translation.src_text: Bèf a ke pa janbe dife.
translation.tgt_text: An ox with a tail does not walk over the fire.

src_text: "Bèf a ke pa janbe dife." (A cow with a tail won’t jump over fire.)

translation.src_text: Bèf dèyè bwè pi bon dlo (si rete dlo).
translation.tgt_text: The ox that comes last drinks better water (if there is still water).

src_text: Bèf dèyè bwè pi bon dlo (the cow that comes last drinks the best water, if any water is left).

translation.src_text: Bèf pa di savann mèsi.
translation.tgt_text: The ox does not thank the field.

src_text: "Bèf pa di savann mèsi." (You don’t thank the pasture that feeds you.)

translation.src_text: Bèf san ke, Bondye pouse mouch pou yo.
translation.tgt_text: The ox with no tail, God will clear the flies for it.

src_text: "Bèf san ke, Bondye pouse mouch pou yo." (Even a cow without a tail, God sends flies for it.)

translation.src_text: Bèl anfòm pa vle di lasante.
translation.tgt_text: Pretty and in shape do not mean healthy.

src_text: "Bèl anfòm pa vle di lasante." (Looking good doesn’t mean you’re healthy.)

translation.src_text: Bèl antèman pa vle di paradi.
translation.tgt_text: A nice funeral does not mean access to paradise.

src_text: "Bèl antèman pa vle di paradi." (A beautiful funeral doesn’t mean paradise.)

translation.src_text: Bèl cheve pa lajan.
translation.tgt_text: Nice hair is not money.

src_text: Bèl cheve pa lajan. (Pretty hair isn’t money.)

translation.src_text: Bèl dan pa vle di zanmi : dan pa kè.
translation.tgt_text: Beautiful smiles do not mean friends: smiles are not the heart.

src_text: "Bèl dan pa vle di zanmi : dan pa kè." (A pretty smile doesn’t mean friendship; teeth are not the heart.)

translation.src_text: Bo nan bouch, men pè dan.
translation.tgt_text: Kiss the mouth, but fear the teeth.

src_text: "Bo nan bouch, men pè dan." (A kiss on the mouth, but afraid of the teeth.)

translation.src_text: Bondye bon.
translation.tgt_text: God is good. (God willing)

src_text: Bondye bon. (God is good.)

translation.src_text: Bondye pa bòpè.
translation.tgt_text: God is not a father-in-law.

src_text: "Bondye pa bòpè." (God is not a stepfather.)

translation.src_text: Bonjou w se paspò ou.
translation.tgt_text: Your greeting is your passport.

src_text: Bonjou w se paspò ou. (Your greeting is your passport.)

translation.src_text: Bouch granmoun santi, sa k ladan se rezon.
translation.tgt_text: Old folk’s breath may stink, what comes out though is wisdom.

src_text: "Bouch granmoun santi, sa k ladan se rezon." (An elder’s mouth may smell, but what comes out of it is wisdom.)

translation.src_text: Bouch manje tout manje, men li pa pale tout pawòl.
translation.tgt_text: The mouth eats all food, but does not talk all words.

src_text: "Bouch manje tout manje, men li pa pale tout pawòl." (A mouth can eat all kinds of food, but it doesn’t speak every word.)

translation.src_text: Bourik fè pitit pou do l ka poze.
translation.tgt_text: The donkey has offspring so that its back may rest.

src_text: "Bourik fè pitit pou do l ka poze." (A donkey has offspring so its back can get some rest.)

translation.src_text: Bourik toujou aji bourik.
translation.tgt_text: A donkey always acts like a donkey.

src_text: Bourik toujou aji bourik. (A donkey always acts like a donkey.)

translation.src_text: Bout kouto miyò pase zong.
translation.tgt_text: A piece of a knife is better than nails.

src_text: "Bout kouto miyò pase zong." (A knife’s edge is better than a fingernail.)

translation.src_text: Bwè dlo nan vè : respekte vè.
translation.tgt_text: Drink water in a glass: respect the glass.

src_text: Bwè dlo nan vè : respekte vè. (When you drink water from a glass, respect the glass.)

translation.src_text: Byen mal pa lanmò.
translation.tgt_text: Not well is not death.

src_text: "Byen mal pa lanmò." (Things may be bad, but they are not the end of the world.)

translation.src_text: Byen prese pa rive.(ou byen: Twò prese pa fe jou louvri)
translation.tgt_text: In a hurry will not arrive.

src_text: Byen prese pa rive. (Haste doesn’t get you there.)

translation.src_text: Byen pre pa lakay.
translation.tgt_text: Being close to home is not the same as being home.

src_text: "Byen pre pa lakay." (Being close by doesn’t mean it’s home.)

translation.src_text: Chaj ou pa ka pòte, ou mete-l atè dousman.
translation.tgt_text: The load you cannot carry, you put it down carefully.

src_text: "Chaj ou pa ka pòte, ou mete-l atè dousman." (If the load is too heavy to carry, you set it down gently.)

translation.src_text: Chak chen pipi jan li konnen.
translation.tgt_text: Every dog pisses his own way.

src_text: "Chak chen pipi jan li konnen." (Everyone does things their own way.)

translation.src_text: Chak kochon gen samdi pa-l.
translation.tgt_text: Each pig gets his own Saturday.

src_text: "Chak kochon gen samdi pa-l." (Everyone gets their own day; what goes around comes around.)

translation.src_text: Chanje mèt, chanje metye.
translation.tgt_text: Trade the boss, trade the job.

src_text: Chanje mèt, chanje metye. (New boss, new trade.)

translation.src_text: Chat mande swe, ou mete chen deyè-l.
translation.tgt_text: If the cat wants to sweat, you seek the dog on it.

src_text: Chat mande swe, ou mete chen deyè-l. (When the cat asks for trouble, you put the dog behind it.)

translation.src_text: Chay sòti sou tèt, li tonbe sou zepòl.
translation.tgt_text: The load that you bear on your head falls on your shoulders.

src_text: "Chay sòti sou tèt, li tonbe sou zepòl." (When a burden leaves the head, it falls on the shoulders.)

translation.src_text: Chemen bezwen pa janm long.
translation.tgt_text: The road to need is never long.

src_text: "Chemen bezwen pa janm long." (When you’re in need, the road never feels long.)

translation.src_text: Chemen bouton se chemen maleng.
translation.tgt_text: The road of a pimple is the road to sores.

src_text: "Chemen bouton se chemen maleng." (The path of a boil is the path of pain.)

translation.src_text: Chemen lajan pa gen pikan.
translation.tgt_text: The money road has no thorns.

src_text: "Chemen lajan pa gen pikan." (The road to money has no thorns.)

translation.src_text: Chemen long pa touye moun.
translation.tgt_text: A long road does not kill people.

src_text: "Chemen long pa touye moun." (A long road doesn’t kill a person.)

translation.src_text: Chen gen kat pye, men li ka mache nan yon sèl chimen.
translation.tgt_text: A dog has four legs, but it walks in only one path.

src_text: "Chen gen kat pye, men li ka mache nan yon sèl chimen." (A dog has four legs, but it can still walk only one path.)

translation.src_text: Chen grangou pa kouche.
translation.tgt_text: A starving dog does not lie down.

src_text: "Chen grangou pa kouche." (A hungry dog won’t lie down.)

translation.src_text: Chen ki gen zo nan bouch li pa gen zanmi.
translation.tgt_text: A dog with a bone in his mouth has no friends.

src_text: "Chen ki gen zo nan bouch li pa gen zanmi." (A dog with a bone in its mouth has no friends.)

translation.src_text: Chen ou fè byen, lè li anraje, se ou li mòde.
translation.tgt_text: The dog that you took care of will bite you when enraged.

src_text: "Chen ou fè byen, lè li anraje, se ou li mòde." (When you treat a dog well, if it gets angry, it’s you it bites.)

translation.src_text: Chen vòle tabak menm si li pa fimen.
translation.tgt_text: The dog steals tobacco even if it does not smoke.

src_text: "Chen vòle tabak menm si li pa fimen." (A dog may steal tobacco even if it doesn’t smoke.)

translation.src_text: Chodyè ou pa monte, ou pa desann li.
translation.tgt_text: The pot you did not put up, you do not put down.

src_text: "Chodyè ou pa monte, ou pa desann li." (If you didn’t put the pot on the fire, you shouldn’t take it off.)

translation.src_text: Chwal ki gen dis mèt mouri nan poto
translation.tgt_text: A horse with ten masters will die [tied] to its post.

src_text: Chwal ki gen dis mèt mouri nan poto (A horse with ten owners dies tied to the post)

translation.src_text: Chwal konn longè kòd li.
translation.tgt_text: The horse knows the length of its rope.

src_text: "Chwal konn longè kòd li." (A horse knows the length of its own rope.)

translation.src_text: Chak pain gen fromagge li
translation.tgt_text: Every bread has it’s cheese.

src_text: "Chak pain gen fromagge li" (Every loaf has its own cheese.)

translation.src_text: Dan pouri gen fòs sou bannann mi.
translation.tgt_text: Rotten teeth only have power over (can only bite) ripe plantains.

src_text: "Dan pouri gen fòs sou bannann mi." (A rotten tooth can still bite into a ripe banana.)

translation.src_text: Dan griyen se danje.
translation.tgt_text: The teeth laugh, beware.

src_text: "Dan griyen se danje." (A grinning tooth can be dangerous.)

translation.src_text: Dan se zo.
translation.tgt_text: Teeth are bones.

src_text: Dan se zo. (Teeth are bones.)

translation.src_text: De kòk kalite pa rete nan menm baskou.
translation.tgt_text: Two good cocks do not stay in the same farm-yard.

src_text: "De kòk kalite pa rete nan menm baskou." (Two roosters of the same kind don’t stay in the same basket.)

translation.src_text: De mèg pa fri.
translation.tgt_text: Two skinny people don’t fry.

src_text: De mèg pa fri. (Two skinny people don’t make a feast.)

translation.src_text: De toro pa rete nan menm savann.
translation.tgt_text: Two bulls do not stay in the same field.

src_text: "De toro pa rete nan menm savann." (Two bulls do not stay in the same pasture.)

translation.src_text: Degaje pa peche.
translation.tgt_text: To get by is not a sin.

src_text: "Degaje pa peche." (Making do is not a sin.)

translation.src_text: Depi nan Ginen, nèg rayi nèg.
translation.tgt_text: Since Africa (Guinea), negros hate negros

src_text: Depi nan Ginen, nèg rayi nèg. (Since the days of Guinea, Black people have hated on each other.)

translation.src_text: Depi ou nan labatwa, fòk ou aksepte san vole sou ou.
translation.tgt_text: If you are in the slaughterhouse, you must accept to get blood on you.

src_text: Depi ou nan labatwa, fòk ou aksepte san vole sou ou. (If you’re in the slaughterhouse, you have to accept that blood will splash on you.)

translation.src_text: Di djab bonjou, lap manje w. Pa di l bonjou, lap manje w.
translation.tgt_text: Greet the devil, he’ll eat you. Don’t greet the devil, he’ll eat you.

src_text: "Di djab bonjou, lap manje w. Pa di l bonjou, lap manje w." (Whether you greet the devil or not, he’ll still eat you.)

translation.src_text: Djòl fè dèt, dèyè peye.
translation.tgt_text: The mouth makes debt, the behind pays back.

src_text: "Djòl fè dèt, dèyè peye." (Talk is cheap; the one who talks has to pay up later.)

translation.src_text: Dlo pa janbe trou.
translation.tgt_text: Water does not cross over holes.

src_text: "Dlo pa janbe trou." (Water doesn’t cross a hole.)

translation.src_text: Doktè pa janm trete tèt li.
translation.tgt_text: The doctor never treats himself.

src_text: Doktè pa janm trete tèt li. (A doctor never treats himself.)

translation.src_text: Doktè pran swen ou, men li pa Bondye.
translation.tgt_text: The doctor takes care of you but he is not God.

src_text: "Doktè pran swen ou, men li pa Bondye." (The doctor can care for you, but he is not God.)

translation.src_text: Dòmi se ti frè lanmò.
translation.tgt_text: Sleep is death’s little brother.

src_text: Dòmi se ti frè lanmò. (Sleep is death’s little brother.)

translation.src_text: Douz metye, trèz mizè.
translation.tgt_text: Twelve trades, thirteen miseries.

src_text: "Douz metye, trèz mizè." (Jack of all trades, master of none.)

translation.src_text: Dwèt ou santi, men ou pa koupe-l jete.
translation.tgt_text: Your finger may smell, but you do not cut it and throw it away.

src_text: "Dwèt ou santi, men ou pa koupe-l jete." (If your finger is hurting, you don’t cut it off and throw it away.)

translation.src_text: Deye mòn gen mòn
translation.tgt_text: Behind mountains there are mountains.

src_text: "Deye mòn gen mòn" (Beyond every mountain, there is another mountain.)

translation.src_text: De (2) twou manti pa fon.
translation.tgt_text: Falsehood has a very weak foundation.

src_text: De (2) twou manti pa fon. (Two lies don’t make a truth.)

translation.src_text: Envite miyò pase mande padon.
translation.tgt_text: To avoid is better than to ask forgiveness.

src_text: "Envite miyò pase mande padon." (It’s better to ask first than to apologize later.)

translation.src_text: "Chak fou gen mawòt li"
translation.tgt_text: Every fool has his hobby

src_text: "Chak fou gen mawòt li" (Every fool has their own way of doing things.)

translation.src_text: Fanm pa dra.
translation.tgt_text: Women are not bed sheets.

src_text: Fanm pa dra. (A woman is not a doormat.)

translation.src_text: Fanm se kajou: plis li vye, plis li bon.
translation.tgt_text: A woman is like mahogany: the older she is, the better she is.

src_text: "Fanm se kajou: plis li vye, plis li bon." (A woman is like cashew: the older she gets, the better she becomes.)

translation.src_text: Fè zanmi ak kouto avan zabriko mi.
translation.tgt_text: Make friend with the knife before apricots are ripe.

src_text: Fè zanmi ak kouto avan zabriko mi. (Make friends with the knife before the apricot ripens.)

translation.src_text: Fèy mapou sanble fèy manyòk.
translation.tgt_text: The ‘Mapou’ leaf looks like the manioc leaf.

src_text: Fèy mapou sanble fèy manyòk. (Maple leaves and cassava leaves can look alike.)

translation.src_text: Fizi tire, nanpwen aranjman.
translation.tgt_text: [When] the guns fire, there is no [possible] agreement.

src_text: Fizi tire, nanpwen aranjman. (Once the shot is fired, there’s no fixing it.)

translation.src_text: Fòk de klòch sonnen pou konn verite-a.
translation.tgt_text: [You must hear] two bells ring to learn the truth.

src_text: Fòk de klòch sonnen pou konn verite-a. (You need to hear both sides to know the truth.)

translation.src_text: Fòk gen maladi pou gen lanmò.
translation.tgt_text: There must be illness so as to have death.

src_text: "Fòk gen maladi pou gen lanmò." (There has to be sickness before there can be death.)

translation.src_text: Fòk ou bat tanbou-a pou tande son li.
translation.tgt_text: You must beat the drum to hear its sound.

src_text: Fòk ou bat tanbou-a pou tande son li. (You have to strike the drum to hear its sound.)

translation.src_text: Fòk ou pèdi tan pou ou gen tan.
translation.tgt_text: You need to lose time in order to have time.

src_text: Fòk ou pèdi tan pou ou gen tan. (You have to lose time in order to have time.)

translation.src_text: Grangou se mizè, vant plen se traka.
translation.tgt_text: Hunger is misery; a full stomach is worriness.

src_text: Grangou se mizè, vant plen se traka. (Hunger is misery, and a full belly brings its own troubles.)

translation.src_text: Ipokrit se kouto de bò.
translation.tgt_text: Hypocrites are two-edge knifes.

src_text: Ipokrit se kouto de bò. (A hypocrite is a double-edged knife.)

translation.src_text: Jan chat mache, se pa konsa li kenbe rat.
translation.tgt_text: The way the cat walks is not the way it holds the rat.

src_text: Jan chat mache, se pa konsa li kenbe rat. (You can’t catch a rat by walking like a cat.)

translation.src_text: Jan ou bat tanbou, se konsa nou danse.
translation.tgt_text: The way you beat the drum is how we dance.

src_text: "Jan ou bat tanbou, se konsa nou danse." (As you beat the drum, so we dance.)

translation.src_text: Jan ou vini se jan an yo resevwa ou.
translation.tgt_text: The way you come is the way people will receive you.

src_text: Jan ou vini se jan an yo resevwa ou. (The way you come is the way people receive you.)

translation.src_text: Je wè, bouch be.
translation.tgt_text: The eyes see, the mouth is silent.

src_text: Je wè, bouch be. (Seeing is one thing, but keeping quiet is another.)

translation.src_text: Jijman Bondye vini sou bourik.
translation.tgt_text: God’s judgment comes on a donkey.

src_text: "Jijman Bondye vini sou bourik." (God’s judgment comes on a donkey.)

translation.src_text: Joumou pa donnen kalbas.
translation.tgt_text: A pumpkin does not bear gourds.

src_text: "Joumou pa donnen kalbas." (A pumpkin doesn’t bear calabashes.)

translation.src_text: Jwe ak makak, men pa manyen ke-l.
translation.tgt_text: [You may] play with the monkey, but don’t play with its tail.

src_text: Jwe ak makak, men pa manyen ke-l. (You can play around with a monkey, but don’t touch its tail.)

translation.src_text: Kalbas gran bouch pa kenbe dlo.
translation.tgt_text: A large pot without cover does not hold water.

src_text: Kalbas gran bouch pa kenbe dlo. (A wide-mouthed calabash can’t hold water.)

translation.src_text: Kat je kontre, manti kaba.
translation.tgt_text: face to face we meet, no lies.

src_text: "Kat je kontre, manti kaba." (When four eyes meet, the lies stop.)

translation.src_text: Kay piti, ou prann nat ou anba bra ou.
translation.tgt_text: [When] the house is small, you hold your bedding under your arm.

src_text: Kay piti, ou prann nat ou anba bra ou. (When the house is small, you have to carry your mat under your arm.)

translation.src_text: Kay koule tronpe soley men li pa tronpe lapli.
translation.tgt_text: A leaking roof may fool sunny weather, but cannot fool the rain.

src_text: "Kay koule tronpe soley men li pa tronpe lapli." (A leaky house may fool the sun, but it can’t fool the rain.)

translation.src_text: Kòfrefò pa swiv kòbiya.
translation.tgt_text: The safe does not follow the hearse.

src_text: "Kòfrefò pa swiv kòbiya." (A stubborn person doesn’t follow just anyone.)

translation.src_text: Komansman chante se soufle.
translation.tgt_text: The first steps of singing are breath.

src_text: "Komansman chante se soufle." (Starting to sing is like taking a breath.)

translation.src_text: Konmisyon pa chaj.
translation.tgt_text: An errand is not a load.

src_text: Konmisyon pa chaj. (A message isn’t a burden.)

translation.src_text: Kote fil fini, se la kouti fini.
translation.tgt_text: Where the thread ends is where the seam ends.

src_text: "Kote fil fini, se la kouti fini." (Where the thread ends, that’s where the sewing stops.)

translation.src_text: Kote ki gen grangou, kabrit pa mouri nan kòd.
translation.tgt_text: Where there is hunger, goats do not die tied to their ropes.

src_text: Kote ki gen grangou, kabrit pa mouri nan kòd. (Where there’s hunger, even a goat tied up won’t die.)

translation.src_text: Kote ki gen granmoun, kay pa boule.
translation.tgt_text: Where there are elders, the house do not burn.

src_text: Kote ki gen granmoun, kay pa boule. (Where there are elders, the house does not burn.)

translation.src_text: Kote ki gen kou pa gen chenn, kote ki gen chenn nanpwen kou.
translation.tgt_text: Where there are blows, there are no chains; where there are chains, there are no blows.

src_text: Kote ki gen kou pa gen chenn, kote ki gen chenn nanpwen kou. (Where there are necks, there are no chains; where there are chains, there are no necks.)

translation.src_text: Kote y’ap plimen kòdenn, poul pa ri.
translation.tgt_text: Where they pluck turkeys, chickens do not laugh.

src_text: Kote y’ap plimen kòdenn, poul pa ri. (When they’re plucking the guinea fowl, the chicken doesn’t laugh.)

translation.src_text: Koulèv ki vle gwo rete nan trou-l.
translation.tgt_text: The snake that wants to get big stays in its hole.

src_text: Koulèv ki vle gwo rete nan trou-l. (A snake that wants to grow big stays in its hole.)

translation.src_text: Kouto pa janm grate manch li.
translation.tgt_text: A knife never scrubs its own handle.

src_text: "Kouto pa janm grate manch li." (A knife never scratches its own handle.)

translation.src_text: Krapo fè kòlè, li mouri san dèyè.
translation.tgt_text: A toad gets angry, it dies without its buttock.

src_text: Krapo fè kòlè, li mouri san dèyè. (When a frog gets angry, it dies without a tail.)

translation.src_text: Labou rete kouran.
translation.tgt_text: The mud stops the flow.

src_text: "Labou rete kouran." (Mud keeps flowing.)

translation.src_text: Lajan kase wòch.
translation.tgt_text: Money breaks rocks.

src_text: Lajan kase wòch. (Money can break rocks.)

translation.src_text: Lamepriz vo mye ke larepons.
translation.tgt_text: Contempt is better than an answer.

src_text: Lamepriz vo mye ke larepons. (Silence is better than a response.)

translation.src_text: Lane pase toujou pi bon.
translation.tgt_text: ‘Last year’ is always better.

src_text: "Lane pase toujou pi bon." (The past year always seems better.)

translation.src_text: Lang pa lanmè, men li ka neye-w.
translation.tgt_text: The tongue is not the sea, but it can drown you.

src_text: "Lang pa lanmè, men li ka neye-w." (Words aren’t the ocean, but they can still drown you.)

translation.src_text: Lè kabrit gen twòp mèt, li mouri nan solèy.
translation.tgt_text: When a goat has too many masters (owners), it dies (tied) in the sun.

src_text: Lè kabrit gen twòp mèt, li mouri nan solèy. (When too many people try to run one thing, it ends up neglected and suffers.)

translation.src_text: Lè labouyi cho, ou manje-l a rebò.
translation.tgt_text: When the porridge is hot, you eat it on the side.

src_text: Lè labouyi cho, ou manje-l a rebò. (When the porridge is hot, you eat it at the edge.)

translation.src_text: Lè pyebwa jwe ak van, li pèdi fèy li.
translation.tgt_text: When the tree plays with the wind, it loses its leaves.

src_text: Lè pyebwa jwe ak van, li pèdi fèy li. (When a tree plays with the wind, it loses its leaves.)

translation.src_text: Lè setan ou echi (lè ou fin’ fè tan ou), se ale p’ou ale.
translation.tgt_text: When your seven years are over (when your time is done), you [must] go for good.

src_text: Lè setan ou echi (lè ou fin’ fè tan ou), se ale p’ou ale. (When your time is up, you have to go.)

translation.src_text: Lè w’ap neye, ou kenbe branch ou jwenn.
translation.tgt_text: When you are drowning, you hang to the branch you reach.

src_text: Lè w’ap neye, ou kenbe branch ou jwenn. (When you’re drowning, you grab whatever branch you can find.)

translation.src_text: Lè yon chodyè cho, ou pa desann li ak men.
translation.tgt_text: When a pot is hot, you do not take it down with your hands.

src_text: Lè yon chodyè cho, ou pa desann li ak men. (When a pot is hot, you don’t handle it with your bare hands.)

translation.src_text: Lespwa fè viv.
translation.tgt_text: Hope makes one live.

src_text: Lespwa fè viv. (Hope keeps you going.)

translation.src_text: M’pat manje pwa, m’pa ka poupou pwa.
translation.tgt_text: I did not eat beans, I cannot poop beans.

src_text: M’pat manje pwa, m’pa ka poupou pwa. (I didn’t eat the beans, so I can’t be the one to poop beans.)

translation.src_text: Machann nan mache gen de mezi.
translation.tgt_text: The merchant at the market has two measures.

src_text: Machann nan mache gen de mezi. (A market seller has two standards.)

translation.src_text: Mache dousman, ou pòte bon nouvèl.
translation.tgt_text: Walk slowly [when] you bear good news.

src_text: Mache dousman, ou pòte bon nouvèl. (Go slowly, and you bring good news.)

translation.src_text: Madichon ou bay bèlmè ou se manman ou li rive.
translation.tgt_text: When you curse your stepmother, your mother will be the victim.

src_text: Madichon ou bay bèlmè ou se manman ou li rive. (The curse you send to your mother-in-law ends up reaching your own mother.)

translation.src_text: Maladi pa konn vanyan.
translation.tgt_text: Illness does not know brave heart.

src_text: Maladi pa konn vanyan. (Illness doesn’t care how strong you are.)

translation.src_text: Malè avèti pa touye kokobe.
translation.tgt_text: A foreseen disaster does not kill the fool.

src_text: "Malè avèti pa touye kokobe." (A warning of trouble doesn’t kill the crippled.)

translation.src_text: Malè pa gen klaksonn.
translation.tgt_text: Misfortune has no horn.

src_text: Malè pa gen klaksonn. (Trouble doesn’t honk its horn.)

translation.src_text: Vye nèg pa vye chen.
translation.tgt_text: An old man is not an old dog.

src_text: "Vye nèg pa vye chen." (An old man is not an old dog.)

translation.src_text: Manje kwit pa gen mèt.
translation.tgt_text: Cooked food has no master.

src_text: Manje kwit pa gen mèt. (Once food is cooked, it belongs to no one.)

translation.src_text: Mapou tonbe, kabrit manje fèy li.
translation.tgt_text: When the ‘Mapou’ [huge tree] is down, the goats eat its leaves.

src_text: "Mapou tonbe, kabrit manje fèy li." (When the mapou tree falls, the goats eat its leaves.)

translation.src_text: Marengwen mòde-w sou nen, men ou pa ka ba-l kou fò.
translation.tgt_text: The mosquito bites you on the nose, but you cannot hit it hard.

src_text: Marengwen mòde-w sou nen, men ou pa ka ba-l kou fò. (If a mosquito bites you on the nose, you can’t really hit it hard.)

translation.src_text: Memwa se paswa.
translation.tgt_text: Memory is a strainer.

src_text: Memwa se paswa. (Memory is a sieve.)

translation.src_text: Menm nan lanfè gen mounpa.
translation.tgt_text: Even in hell, there are people from your clan.

src_text: Menm nan lanfè gen mounpa. (Even in hell, there are people you know.)

translation.src_text: Mennen koulèv al lekòl pa anyen; se fè-l chita ki rèd.
translation.tgt_text: To take the snake to school is nothing; it is to make it sit that is tough.

src_text: "Mennen koulèv al lekòl pa anyen; se fè-l chita ki rèd." (Taking a snake to school is nothing; the hard part is making it sit still.)

translation.src_text: Mèt do pa grate do.
translation.tgt_text: You cannot scratch your own back.

src_text: "Mèt do pa grate do." (You scratch my back, I scratch yours.)

translation.src_text: Mezire avan ou koupe.
translation.tgt_text: Measure before you cut.

src_text: Mezire avan ou koupe. (Measure twice before you cut.)

translation.src_text: Mouch pa bezwen vyann, men li gate-l.
translation.tgt_text: The fly does not need the meat, but it will spoil it.

src_text: "Mouch pa bezwen vyann, men li gate-l." (A fly doesn’t need meat, but it ruins it.)

translation.src_text: Moun ki bezwen deyò chache chemen pòt.
translation.tgt_text: He who must go out search for the door.

src_text: Moun ki bezwen deyò chache chemen pòt. (If you need to go outside, you find a way out.)

translation.src_text: Moun mouri pa konnen valè dra blan.
translation.tgt_text: The dead does not know the value of white sheets.

src_text: "Moun mouri pa konnen valè dra blan." (The dead don’t know the value of a white sheet.)

translation.src_text: Moun mouri pa pè santi.
translation.tgt_text: The dead is not afraid to smell.

src_text: Moun mouri pa pè santi. (The dead don’t fear the smell.)

translation.src_text: Moun pa konn achte chat nan sak.
translation.tgt_text: People don’t buy a cat in a bag.

src_text: Moun pa konn achte chat nan sak. (People don’t buy a cat in a bag.)

translation.src_text: Moun pa-w se dra.
translation.tgt_text: Your clan is sheets.

src_text: Moun pa-w se dra. (Your people are like a blanket.)

translation.src_text: Move zèb ka leve toupatou.
translation.tgt_text: Weeds can grow anywhere.

src_text: "Move zèb ka leve toupatou." (Bad grass can grow everywhere.)

translation.src_text: Nan bay kout men, ou jwenn kout pye
translation.tgt_text: You give a hand, but [you may] get kicked out.

src_text: "Nan bay kout men, ou jwenn kout pye" (When you lend a helping hand, you may get kicked in return)

translation.src_text: Nan mitan diri, ti wòch goute grès.
translation.tgt_text: In the middle of [cooked] rice, a little pebble will taste grease.

src_text: "Nan mitan diri, ti wòch goute grès." (In the middle of rice, even a small stone gets coated with grease.)

translation.src_text: Nan mitan avèg, bògn se rwa.
translation.tgt_text: Among the blind, the one-eyed is king.

src_text: Nan mitan avèg, bògn se rwa. (Among the blind, the one-eyed man is king.)

translation.src_text: Nanpwen cho ki pa vin frèt..
translation.tgt_text: There is nothing hot that will not get cold.

src_text: Nanpwen cho ki pa vin frèt.. (Nothing hot stays hot forever.)

translation.src_text: Nanpwen metye ki pa nouri mèt li..
translation.tgt_text: There is no craft that will not feed the craftsman.

src_text: Nanpwen metye ki pa nouri mèt li.. (There’s no trade that doesn’t feed its master.)

translation.src_text: Nèg fè lide-l, Bondye ba-l dwa.
translation.tgt_text: The man gets the idea, God authorizes it.

src_text: "Nèg fè lide-l, Bondye ba-l dwa." (When a man makes up his mind, God gives him the right.)

translation.src_text: Nen pran kou, je kouri dlo; je pran kou, nen kouri dlo.
translation.tgt_text: The nose is hurt, the eyes water; the eyes are hurt, the nose runs.

src_text: "Nen pran kou, je kouri dlo; je pran kou, nen kouri dlo." (When the nose gets hit, the eyes run with tears; when the eyes get hit, the nose runs with tears.)

translation.src_text: Nou léd, nou la.
translation.tgt_text: We are ugly, but we are here.

src_text: "Nou léd, nou la." (We’re here, we’re still standing.)

translation.src_text: Ou bat tanbou epi ou danse ankò.
translation.tgt_text: You beat the drum and you dance again.

src_text: Ou bat tanbou epi ou danse ankò. (You beat the drum and then you dance again.)

translation.src_text: Ou granmoun sèlman lè ou lakay ou.
translation.tgt_text: You are an old man only when you are at home.

src_text: "Ou granmoun sèlman lè ou lakay ou." (You’re only really grown when you’re at home.)

translation.src_text: Ou konn kouri, men fòk ou konn kache.
translation.tgt_text: You [may] know how to run, but you must know how to hide.

src_text: Ou konn kouri, men fòk ou konn kache. (You may know how to run, but you also need to know how to hide.)

translation.src_text: Ou konn sa w’ap kite; ou pa konn sa ou pral jwenn.
translation.tgt_text: You [may] know what you leave behind; you do not know what you will get.

src_text: Ou konn sa w’ap kite; ou pa konn sa ou pral jwenn. (You know what you’re leaving behind; you don’t know what you’re going to find.)

translation.src_text: Ou pa fouye zo nan kalalou.
translation.tgt_text: You do not dig up bones in akra.

src_text: Ou pa fouye zo nan kalalou. (Don’t go looking for trouble where there isn’t any.)

translation.src_text: Ou pa dwè dekouvri Sen Pòl pou kouvri Sen Piè.
translation.tgt_text: You must not undress Saint Paul to dress Saint Peter.

src_text: Ou pa dwè dekouvri Sen Pòl pou kouvri Sen Piè. (You shouldn’t uncover Saint Paul just to cover Saint Peter.)

translation.src_text: Ou pa ka fè san sòti nan wòch.
translation.tgt_text: You cannot have blood flow from a rock.

src_text: Ou pa ka fè san sòti nan wòch. (You can’t get blood from a stone.)

translation.src_text: Ougan pa janm geri maleng li.
translation.tgt_text: The ‘ougan’ (Medecine Man) never cures his own illness.

src_text: Ougan pa janm geri maleng li. (A healer never heals his own wounds.)

translation.src_text: Ouvriye vann zouti-l, men li pa vann metye-l.
translation.tgt_text: A carpenter [may] sell his tools, but he [cannot] sell his skills.

src_text: Ouvriye vann zouti-l, men li pa vann metye-l. (A worker may sell his tools, but he doesn’t sell his trade.)

translation.src_text: Pa bay bèf la babokèt lè l’ap rale kabwèt.
translation.tgt_text: Do not put the harness on the ox when it is going to pull the kart.

src_text: Pa bay bèf la babokèt lè l’ap rale kabwèt. (Don’t put a muzzle on the ox while it’s pulling the cart.)

translation.src_text: Pa jete vye chodyè pou chodyè nèf.
translation.tgt_text: Don’t throw away the old pot for a new pot.

src_text: Pa jete vye chodyè pou chodyè nèf. (Don’t throw away an old pot for a new one.)

translation.src_text: Pa kroke makout twò wo, men kote men ou ka rive.
translation.tgt_text: Do not hang the basket too high, but where your hand can reach it.

src_text: Pa kroke makout twò wo, men kote men ou ka rive. (Don’t hang your bag too high, but where your hand can reach.)

translation.src_text: Pa pale sa ou pa we ak prop je ou.
translation.tgt_text: Never talk about something that you have not seen with your own eyes.

src_text: Pa pale sa ou pa we ak prop je ou. (Don’t speak on what you haven’t seen with your own eyes.)

translation.src_text: Pa pèdi founo pou yon sèl pen.
translation.tgt_text: Do not lose your oven over just one bread.

src_text: Pa pèdi founo pou yon sèl pen. (Don’t lose the whole oven over one loaf of bread.)

translation.src_text: Padon pa geri maleng.
translation.tgt_text: Forgiveness does not cure illness.

src_text: "Padon pa geri maleng." (Forgiveness doesn’t heal the wound.)

translation.src_text: Pale franse pa di lespri pou sa.
translation.tgt_text: To speak French does not mean wits.

src_text: "Pale franse pa di lespri pou sa." (Speaking French doesn’t necessarily mean someone is smart.)

translation.src_text: Parese pa gen kay.
translation.tgt_text: Lazy people do not have a house.

src_text: Parese pa gen kay. (Laziness doesn’t build a home.)

translation.src_text: Paròl gen zèl.
translation.tgt_text: Words have wings.

src_text: Paròl gen zèl. (Words travel fast.)

translation.src_text: Parol pa chay.
translation.tgt_text: Words are not a load.

src_text: Parol pa chay. (Words don’t weigh anything.)

translation.src_text: Paròl two fò, machwè gonfle.
translation.tgt_text: Too false words [make] the jaw swell.

src_text: Paròl two fò, machwè gonfle. (Too much talking gets you in trouble.)

translation.src_text: Pè pa preche de fwa.
translation.tgt_text: Fear does not preach twice.

src_text: Pè pa preche de fwa. (Fear doesn’t need to be preached twice.)

translation.src_text: Pitit ki pa kriye pa bezwen tete.
translation.tgt_text: The baby who does not cry does not need to be breast-fed.

src_text: "Pitit ki pa kriye pa bezwen tete." (A child who doesn’t cry doesn’t need to be nursed.)

translation.src_text: Pitit tig, se tig.
translation.tgt_text: A tiger cub is a tiger.

src_text: "Pitit tig, se tig." (Like father, like son.)

translation.src_text: Pito ou mize ou nan wout, ou pote bon nouvèl.
translation.tgt_text: Better to take your time on the way, if you bring good news.

src_text: Pito ou mize ou nan wout, ou pote bon nouvèl. (Better to be on the road and bring good news.)

translation.src_text: Pòt tè pa goumen ak pòt fè.
translation.tgt_text: The clay pot [must] not wrestle with the iron pot.

src_text: "Pòt tè pa goumen ak pòt fè." (A clay pot shouldn’t fight with an iron pot.)

translation.src_text: Pousyè pa leve san van.
translation.tgt_text: Dust does not lift without wind.

src_text: Pousyè pa leve san van. (Nothing happens without a cause.)

translation.src_text: Premye so pa so.
translation.tgt_text: The first fall is not a fall

src_text: "Premye so pa so." (The first jump doesn’t count as a real jump.)

translation.src_text: Pye pa gen rasinn : tout moun ka tonbe.
translation.tgt_text: Feet have no roots: everyone can fall.

src_text: Pye pa gen rasinn : tout moun ka tonbe. (No one is rooted forever; everybody can fall.)

translation.src_text: Pye poul pi bon pase bwadann.
translation.tgt_text: A hen’s foot is better than a donkey’s hoof.

src_text: "Pye poul pi bon pase bwadann." (Chicken feet are better than a bad bargain.)

translation.src_text: Gwo non touye ti chen
translation.tgt_text: Too much fame can be bad.
